findings.description: `ensureBrief` now throws `InvalidProfileError` when the brief is a symlink, a hard link or not a regular file. Before, it never threw for these. The `pup brief edit` call site (`src/cli/index.ts:1729`) has no try/catch, and `fatalExitCode` rethrows anything it does not recognise. So an operator who keeps `brief.md` as a symlink into a dotfiles repo (the case the ADR's Cost section names) gets a stack trace instead of the one-line refusal that `brief show` gives for the same error type (`src/cli/index.ts:1709-1716`, decision 57). Separately, `readBrief`'s refusal (lines 109-112) tells the operator to "Replace it with `pup brief edit`", and for a linked brief that command now refuses too. Fix: catch `InvalidProfileError` around `ensureBrief` in the CLI and `refuse(error.message)`.

ADR 0194 says pup writes a store file only by creating a fresh one and names "one write" that skips `writeStoreFile`, but other store writes skip it too and are not listed under Known gaps: the hook's `>>` append to `events.jsonl` (`profile-compiler.service.ts:1323`, which follows a link) and `writeRenamed` in `src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts:1127-1132` (session-env, pane-pid, the socket record). A reader auditing the ADR would take its list as complete. Reword it to "the writes listed here" and add these writes as accepted exceptions.

The `statSync` gap names only `findStalledSessions`, but `dashboard.service.ts:357` has the same link-following `existsSync`/`statSync` on `eventsFile`, for the session's `stalledAt` value. Say "the stall checks".

`readEventsFile` writes out by hand the open (O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK), fstat, isFile and nlink===1 checks that `readPlainFile(path, { followLinks: false, soleLink: true })` from this same PR already does. Reusing it would remove the hand-written block and four fs imports. Before switching, check that a long session's events file stays under readPlainFile's 1 MiB cap, and note that its "not a plain file" error has no `code` to match on.

The new `ELOOP` branches here and in `session-handoff.service.ts` only reword the error, and the file is refused either way. The raw `ELOOP` message already names the file. Dropping the branches removes two branches and the `NodeJS.ErrnoException` casts, but the tests that check these strings would need updating.

The new test file sits next to `capability.utils.ts`, but its mirror `test/unit/adapters/capability-utils.test.ts` already exists (docs/conventions/testing.md §Layout: "One test file per source file, at the path the source has under `src/`"). The `readPlainFile` cases are now split from the rest of that module's tests. Move the two cases into the mirror file.

`refuseLinkedStoreFiles` only checks that `state.db-journal` is a regular file with one link. It doesn't check what's inside. A session can write a plain `-journal` that names a "super-journal" path. When `openStore` next opens the store, SQLite treats the journal as hot and rolls it back, and then deletes whatever file that path names.

refuted_findings.description: `readHandoff` now throws a plain `Error` for a handoff that is a symlink, a hard link, or larger than 1 MiB. Before, it returned the file's text. `isHandoffReady` passes that throw on, so a tampered handoff stops every respawn. The documented contract is that it starts a fresh request instead.
refuted_findings.refutation: ADR 0194:25-28 and 50-51 name the handoff among the reads that must refuse a link, and say its message tells the operator to remove the file and write the handoff again, which this code does. The throw is only reached when the file is swapped after a real handoff-done signal, because markHandoffReady already refuses a linked or oversized file. Once the operator removes the file, the next respawn asks again. That is not decision 49's wedge, which could only be cleared with kill --respawn and lost the handoff. The hash-mismatch refusal in respawnSession already leaves through the same uncaught plain-Error path. Leftover: the isHandoffReady JSDoc (150-155) now overstates the 'fresh request' behaviour.

process_issues.description: The consolidator grouped findings 5, 6 and 9 (ADR write exceptions, ADR statSync gap, session-runtime writeRenamed). The orchestrator merged only 5 and 9 (the same incomplete list of write exceptions) and kept 6 (the stat-read gap) separate, so merged_duplicates is 1.

Two nits about STORE_FILE_SUFFIXES were dropped: conventions said move it to a *.constants.ts, simplicity said inline it. They recommended opposite fixes, both reviewers rated them low confidence, and neither named a concrete cost.
The -journal super-journal finding depends on SQLite pager.c behaviour taken from knowledge of the bundled SQLite version. The CI static review could not read the source or run a test to confirm it.
